steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: The Eye of Iberia. It's been a long, long time since I last set foot here.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Countless soldiers from the Penal Battalion laid down their lives here. And when the Seaborn finally broke through our defense line, countless engineers died in vain inside the lighthouse.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Before our last ship was swallowed, we fled. For every ten men who left home, hardly one returned.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: But now, behold.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Light!
Carmen's voice trembles for the first time in an eternity.
Kal'tsit stares silently out into the center of the distant reef. A massive lighthouse illuminates the entire sky, as bright as the day.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I don't see the ship.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: That is a good sign. It proves they found what they were looking for.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Let's proceed. As long as this light is not extinguished, we will press forward.

steps.name: Sea Terror
steps.text: (Slithers around the main door)

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...Mon3tr.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Screeches)

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Clear the way. We're going in.
The heat of fire.
The Sea Terrors gather around the main door, wandering, spinning.
Carmen's eyes sweep into the distance. They follow a line of the charred corpses of these abominations the entire way, their remains vanishing with the wind.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: The Sea Terrors do not feel fear.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But they do know how to seek advantage and avoid disadvantage. Their base instincts have taught them to hunt cautiously.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: ...They have been taught fear. These creatures may not know what a country is, let alone laws and morals.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: But they have learned to fear the High Inquisitor. They have learned to fear everything we have built on top of civilization.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Dario!
Kal'tsit does not say anything.
She can see. She can see a strange ring on a patch of fluorescent ground.
Charred corpses are stacked high into a mountain. The deaths of tens of thousands of their kin had imprinted a new behavior upon the Sea Terrors—
—Do not approach the lighthouse.
A feeble flame still flickers. It was originally a great bonfire.
Before the Sea Terrors had perished in a tide of death, there was nothing flammable here at all.
At the heart of the flame stands a single man. He lifts his lantern and leans on his sword, just as he did when he learned to stand guard in his youth—motionless.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: You've done well, Dario.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Be at peace now.
The lantern in Dario's hand seems to echo Carmen's farewell. In an instant, the fire swallows even more Sea Terrors before the raging flame then wraps around the silent High Inquisitor.
His already-clouded eyes are still gazing far into the distance.
Carmen remains silent for a long time before Dario's statue-like body.
Kal'tsit does not interrupt Carmen's mourning. She only takes in the scene with her eyes. There aren't many signs of the Hunters' activity here.
The High Inquisitor remained here alone, staving off the surging tides of Sea Terrors until his life was spent.
But even if the soldier's lifeforce had bled dry long ago, the Sea Terrors still feared him. Because his flame had not extinguished, because his light had not dimmed.
The Inquisitor had turned himself into a force of nature, a pledge to defend the sanctity of the Eye of Iberia even beyond death.
After a long time, Carmen lifts his head.

Only then does Kal'tsit see the signs of age in the old man in front of her. Though the Inquisition had used various methods to prolong his life, in this moment he could no longer hide the fatigue in his eyes.
He turns his head and looks towards Kal'tsit, then back to Dario, who was gradually disappearing into the flame.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: He was my finest student, Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We have three minutes to mourn the death of this soldier. Once the flames go out, nothing will stand between the Sea Terrors and their nest. They will swarm this place.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Also, I didn't see the girl. At least his disciple survived.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Are there no higher-level Seaborn here?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Doesn't seem so, for the time being.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Their numbers are nothing to be feared then.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: 'For the time being.'

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We ought to find a more permanent solution. The Eye of Iberia was built by Breogan. It has the potential to become the hub for establishing a link with Ægir.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Assuming they were able to find the ship... Wait, hold on.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Who reactivated the Eye of Iberia? Neither the Ægir nor Dario should've had any experience with this.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...Look up there.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Ugh... Finally...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: *pant*... *pant*... Th-The control panel is fine...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Phew, I'm totally worn out...

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Hums curiously)

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Hwaaaaah—!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Y-You're—

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...I must admit, you've surpassed my expectations.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You managed to re-light the Eye of Iberia by yourself, restoring at least thirty percent of its functionality.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You did this, alone. Under these conditions.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: You... You're the one Mr. Elysium mentioned. Oh!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Wh-What about Mr. Inquisitor?! He's been fighting for his life down there this entire time and I, I didn't dare get close to him since I wouldn't be able to help anyway, so all I could do was keep an eye on the control panel here...

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: He made the ultimate sacrifice.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: What...?

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: But by no means was it in vain. He sacrificed himself for his faith, and as such, will now live on forever.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: He died heroically as an Inquisitor, as a vindicator of Iberia. His ideal self shall be forever enshrined on the coasts of Iberia.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: And then there is you, Ægir. You have defended the purpose of his sacrifice. You have persisted all this time, and never given up.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: You've done well.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I-I never got to talk to him much, but... he... *sob*...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Um... what about Gran Faro? What's going to happen to my home?

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: ...I usually don't answer every question from the general public.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: But for now, I don't intend to lie to you. Gran Faro will soon be under the management of the Penal Battalion. The citizens will all come under their unified control, and contribute to the construction of frontline checkpoints.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Also... Thiago died at the hands of heretics.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: No!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: H-How could this happen? Uncle Thiago, is he really—?!

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: He had long been aware of the Church of the Deep's cultists, yet turned a blind eye to them. His cover-up thwarted the plans of the Penal Battalion, and delayed our ability to send support here.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Even if he'd escaped death, he would not have escaped me, child.
Jordi collapses limply onto the ground.
He feels numb and exhausted. He feels like the single string supporting him through everything that happened, long worn thin, had suddenly snapped.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Uncle Thiago... Why?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...Mon3tr, guard the entrance.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Obeys cheerfully)

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Can you confirm where the Stultifera Navis was last seen?

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Dame Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Not that far. And the last signal came less than forty-eight hours ago.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: What...?

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: She's still able to send signals?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Breogan helped the Iberian royal family construct lighthouses and fleets. Why, if not for restoring a connection to his homeland?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Be it the Eye of Iberia or some transponder hidden in a corner in the Stultifera Navis, they all use the Ægir's technology without reservation.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Of course, all of this assumes that the Seaborn haven't already destroyed the ship or turned it into their nest.
Carmen's eyes silently follow the direction of the light extending towards the horizon.
The Stultifera Navis cannot be seen by the naked eye. The ocean is too expansive, and what's not too far for a ship is still a cruel joke to those on land.
The weary saint once again shows his age. His lips quiver, as if innumerable thoughts are crossing through his mind.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Alfonso... Garcia... Touré... Julia...

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Are you still out there?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: My captain and Gladiia pursued it into the sea.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: We should go help them.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: No, we'd be better off waiting here. The waters are restless, and the Seaborns' scents swirl together. There's probably more than just one.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Did you hear something, Skadi?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: What? No, I didn't.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: I see.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: What have you done to this place?!

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: You, Ægirs, how'd you get in here?

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: I was the only one with the key, and when the ol' deadbeat kicked the bucket, I threw it into the ocean! It's been fifty years already!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: If this is the power source for the vessel, wouldn't locking it up mean giving up hope?

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: The ol' deadbeat was the last engineer we had. When he died, we had nobody left who could fix the ship.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: To make matters worse, we were already tangled up in the Seaborn, and couldn't get away. Didn't need anyone rocking the boat on my watch.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: But answer me! How'd you find this place?!

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Breogan. The captain followed the clues he left, which led to Iberia, then here.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: You people... you know the shipwright?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Nope, not at all. I've always been more into the arts anyway.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: But it really shouldn't come as a surprise. To return to Ægir, we must follow the trail of the Ægir—

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: —What's this?

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Ah, you've even gotten your hands dirty digging up some of Breogan's personal belongings... Hasn't Ægir ever heard of respecting people's privacy?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: What does it say?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Breogan's experiences on land. A travel log, I guess?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Is this what the Captain's been looking for?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: No clue. Why don't you ask her yourself?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: ...Just a small part of it.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Returning empty handed, eh?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: It disappeared.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Furthermore, the reason we didn't chase any further is because there were signs of other Seaborn nearby.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: They came here following distant scents and the calls of their kin.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Now, I don't mind skipping straight to the slaughter. But we should resolve the problem of this ship first.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: You dare treat my Iberia as a prize to be taken?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: This ship is the only way for us to return to Ægir. And only it can contact our cities.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: As for the issue of repairs, perhaps I might be more qualified than a handful of backwards Iberians who know little of Breogan's technology.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I can't pass up this opportunity, even if we must resort to force.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Two against four, eh?

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: (Howls vigilantly) —

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Three against three.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: ...Captain?!

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Not so fast, Gladiia.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Don't forget what I said.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: ...You never gave me a reason to give up on returning to Ægir.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: I'm telling you, you don't know what it's like there now.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: The Seaborn have never taken the initiative to attack our cities unless their nests and living spaces were threatened. Each act of slaughter, each act of destruction, has been fueled by the Ægir's degeneracy.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: They thought we were dead. They lost contact with us. The blood of the Seaborn flow within us.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: In all our long years of battling against these enemies, we finally have a prime opportunity.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: And you think these few acts of 'degeneracy' have nothing to do with the scum we fight? Even if left alone, the Seaborn's living spaces will grow like a tumor until the entire ocean is devoured.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: This and that are two separate issues.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Neither of which can be solved by heading home, rejoining the army, and marching forth once more.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Why don't we try thinking outside the box this time?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: So you've chosen to listen to those lowly beasts, to walk with them, to understand them.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: They call us their kin, but what do we know about them? Far too little.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: I can hardly even understand what I've seen myself. Until we've obtained definite answers about their gods, everything we do is uselessly groping around in the dark.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: What are you talking about, Captain?!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You... You and the Seaborn... How do we know you're still on our side? Why do you have to...

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Every Hunter who thought they could get something out of the Seaborn has ended up disappearing.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Of course, you should understand that better than me.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Their whispers... resonate... They will invade your mind. Those are not your thoughts!

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: ...Skadi.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: That's... also a separate issue. I'll let Gladiia give you the specifics.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Ship captain, escort them away.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: I was just thinking the same thing, Ægir.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: ...What a pity.
Stillness. Silence. Hunters long separated always seem to have the least pleasant of reunions.
Something squirms in the hearts of Skadi and Specter. The chief mate hesitates, its wounds still aching.
Swords are drawn, bowstrings stretched taut.
Quiet.
Too quiet.
Wait, how is this possible? The rushing of the waves, the howling of the wind, the creaking sounds of the hull being torn open by Seaborn—
They all become distant.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Hunters!

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Th-The ship is sailing!

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Nonsense, Old Iberian. Just how many years do you think—

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: No, I swear it's true! Something's pushing the ship, and... it might've been pushing the ship the whole time we were chasing after the Seaborn.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: And... from the very beginning, um...

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Our surroundings have been unusually quiet.

steps.name: Rocinante
steps.text: *Huff*...

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: Kin, gather. Take this cell, and go far away.

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: Follow... We will follow. We will find the end of the storm.

steps.name: Rocinante
steps.text: (Shakes head meekly)

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: The waves are fading.

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: Silence, is coming.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: I don't hear anything at all. After so many years of the waves washing against us, why...?

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Everything, is just like that day...

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: (Cowers in pain and suffering)

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Garcia! Ugh... My hand, it's shaking... Damn it, if I didn't need it to hunt, I would've lopped this thing off a long time ago.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: What's the meaning of this, Ægir?!
Gladiia does not answer.
She imperceptibly reaches for her neck. The scales, the part of her that do not belong to her, are resonating with something.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: The scent of the Seaborn... The smell of the ocean, it's all gone. Look outside. It's way too peaceful.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: How could this be?

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Haah... What's going on? Why's it so quiet?

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: ...Wait.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Did you hear that? What was that?

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Was there something—

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: 'The ocean sank into an unprecedented silence. Anomalies appeared across the shore, as violently ebbing tides and irregular waves heralded the coming of disaster.'

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: 'All sounds were smothered. From waves crashing against the shore to the chiming of city clock towers, all noise faded away.'
Until the voices of the people all disappeared as well.
Until the wind was stilled.
The Profound Silence came without a sound.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Impossible, it's just like in the Inquisition's records. Are we facing... another Silence?!

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Shark, where are you going?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Heading up to check things out.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: I'll go with you.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Me too.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: No, Skadi.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: You and Gladiia stay here.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: ...Skadi.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Stay with Gladiia, and remember this one thing.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: You will always be our Hunter.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Laurentina, let's go.
Specter lifts her head towards the sky.
The dark clouds know not when to dissipate, but she, who has lost the concept of time, finds a sea of stars in the sky.
She can finally hear that voice.
The voice that calls out to her.
Specter paces around the deck, and Ulpianus casts her a concerned glance for just a moment.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: You and the captain have a keen sense of smell. Can you sense any Seaborn around us?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: No, right now, there is little difference between here and the land.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Even though we're clearly floating out at sea. It's disconcerting.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: I'll head the other way to see if we're really being pushed by a current.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: ...See you soon.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: O starry sky.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: This is the first time in many years I've seen the stars so clearly.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: I had forgotten so many things. I forgot my home, was used by others, and what finally saved my life and awakened my memories was the part of me I hated most.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Accepting that I'm a freak actually wasn't as hard as it sounds. That's what makes me unique.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: The one, final thing I am unable to let go of... is my home.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: But have I really returned? Is this place on the sea's surface really Ægir? Is this still my home?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Just because Gladiia never said it doesn't mean I wouldn't realize. It wouldn't be the first time rifts have grown between Hunters, but between us and Ægir? We've been separated by the shore for too long.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: ...I remember something else.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: When I was little, I once went with my parents and grandparents to watch the stars on the ocean's surface adorn the sky, on a day much like this. Even the most beautiful pearl geode couldn't compare to that splendor.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: In retrospect, even after I became a Hunter, I was always leaving my home again and again, but never reaching anywhere else.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Haha... I suppose I'm getting a bit homesick.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Where are you going to take me this time, Amaia?
Under the magnificent starry sky, the creature quietly looks down on Specter.
It makes not a single sound. The ship splitting the waves, the wind's bluster. All sounds are drowned out by His soft murmurs.
He hovers in the air as if walking on water, gently kissing the light of the stars and moons, His tentacles coruscating in a beautiful array.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Nowhere, Laurentina. The ocean is boundless, and wherever we go is all the same.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: I've always been able to hear your song, Amaia.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Laurentina, that is the name of our scaleless kin, the Liberi, the Iberian.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: As I consumed her, she kept stroking my head. She spoke to me of many things. Time itself was like frozen dust, an eternity seeming to pass as I listened to her.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Until she could no longer speak, until even her bones were digested by our smallest kin, she nurtured me with both nutrition and time. She taught me everything I know.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Since when were you so sentimental towards your food?

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Such was her request, I merely granted it. If there is purpose to such emotions, we are willing to experiment.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: What of Ishar'mla? Gladiia? And... Ulpianus?

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Are your kin ready to return to the great sea?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: ...We've had a bit of an internal disagreement.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Why? Your home is clearly right before your eyes. We many are clearly right here awaiting you.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: You're homesick, Laurentina. Amaia told me that, of all the Ægir she ever made contact with, you harbor the greatest affection for Ægir itself.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Come.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Embrace me, and I will bring you back home.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: You know, I've never touched a living Seaborn before. I prefer your kind dead.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Just as you prefer to give shape to inorganic matter, even though it offers nothing for your survival?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Do you have any other pursuits other than 'survival'?

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Pursuits? Like your pursuit to return home?

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: The survival of our kind. The survival of more of us. The survival of we many.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: All beings ought to form a single entity. Life should not be so disorderly.
The Seaborn descends onto the deck.
Specter laughs.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: You're a graceful one. Did Amaia teach you that as well?

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: It was just her request. A memento.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: I suppose that means you'll be paying back both of our debts?

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: ...Ah, before her death, Amaia entrusted you to me. I will make use of your life. I will also fulfill your requests.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Amaia thanks you. She said I should help you. Because of you, their work was able to take another step forward. Their 'research' and 'ideals' have all advanced greatly.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: I can talk to you about Ishar'mla. I can take you back to Ægir. I can share with you where our kind are, and how they are doing. I can name your clansmen who are trying to become one with us.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Amaia begged me to help you. Only through helping you, will you accept us as kin.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: ...Hah.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: In that case, my first request is...

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Stop singing. I want to hear the wind of my hometown.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Very well.
In an instant, the wind and the waves return to Specter's ears.
Just as the sound of the first waves splashing against the deck rings out clearly, Ulpianus's giant blade is already poised above the Seaborn's head.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Die.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: What—?! It managed to block? —Nngh!

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Ulpianus!

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: A sufficiently heavy blow. Our kin in the ocean will welcome his unconscious form. They will take him back to our nest, where we will spend time becoming one with him.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: As for this floating box... it has been used to house our kin who have not yet adapted to the sea. But most of them died, and the rest have refused to become one with us.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Therefore, it is no longer needed.
Specter is unable to see the Seaborn's movements, but like a piece of garbage being swept aside by a pedestrian, the once-glorious cannon mounted on the ship vanishes in the blink of an eye.
A few seconds later, an enormous splash in the distance reveals where the steel construct had gone.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: (How did it manage to slice off that cannon? With its tail?!)

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Shit—
Specter's eyes are unable to follow.
Whether shaken by the ease with which Ulpianus was repelled, or distracted by the sound of the metal cannon being sliced through, Specter is easily struck and sent crashing into the deck.
She was unable to see the attack at all.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Come, let us return to the sea.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Whether to hunt, or to communicate, or to evolve, we must all return to the sea.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Halt!

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: You trying to take apart my ship, you monster?!

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Garcia!

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: (Roars) —!
The chief mate charges at the Seaborn.
But before even laying a finger on that elegant being, the chief mate's movements suddenly freeze.
Kin. This is kin.
I am attacking my own kind?

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: What a paradoxical being. You have consumed many of our kin, yet many more go hungry. You ought to feed them.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Turn into nutrients, and nourish our kind.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Garcia!

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: What are you doing to my chief mate?!

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: —Ugh!

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Gaah... Goddamnit!

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Don't worry, I'm alright... *cough*.

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: Alfonso...

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: What is it...?

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Wait, hold on, what?! Garcia, you—

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: Alfonso.

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: Today is... the last day... of our voyage.

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: All these years... I... always treated myself as... a monster. Easier... that way.

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: I know. If I die... you'll be lonely... and then you'll die. You shouldn't... die... so I'm... worthless.

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: Today is the last day... of our voyage.

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: I... I think I already... feel kinship towards it.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: No! No!

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Garcia! You can still talk! You're still yourself!

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: Time... is up. The Stultifera... will soon sink. The fluorescent sea has already started... to corrode the ship.

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: I—

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: —Will fight to the death, as an Iberian. I will never... accept it as my kin.
The Seaborn has already bent down.
It looks hardly any different from the greatest chief mate Iberia has ever known.
Garcia nudges the shining crown sitting atop its head.

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: (Iberian) My beloved... Remember... your duty.

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: (Roars) —

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: You are not fighting me, Garcia.

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: Graaaaah—

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: You are fighting we many inside your heart. You are on this ship, but you thirst for the sea.

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: Urgh— Hraaaagh—

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: But it doesn't matter.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Become sustenance, and nourish our kin. Or, become one with us.
The Chief Mate's body is punctured, blood gushing out like a spring.
The Seaborn tosses Garcia overboard into the ocean, like chucking out bait.
It gazes from above, noble and impassive, like an inviolable eikon.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: What... What just happened?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: How could it so easily—

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Human, kin, and all living things in between.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Amaia wishes to correct you. And thus, it shall be done. I simply welcome back my kin, and welcome back Ishar-mla.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Protect the lives of our kin. Then, return to we many. 'Return home.'

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Shark.
Gladiia effortlessly steps forward, casting off the gentle beckoning from behind.
In the space of a moment, Skadi, who had been standing behind her, and Specter, once again returning to battle, react in sync and brandish their weapons at the Seaborn.
As the fastest of the group, Gladiia would improve the synergy between the three if she slowed down a bit—but she had already lost the capacity to stay calm.
It dodges. Or more accurately, it simply takes a step forward, but its speed is sufficient.
It has its eyes only on Skadi.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: There are many among us who wish to see you. Ishar-mla. Ishar'mla.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Our kind awaits you. We await you. We hope you will answer our call.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Filth, is there no end to your arrogance?
Gladiia whirls her lance at the Seaborn, but it does not evade. It is run through, its body easily lifted and smashed down into a deep pit.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: No good... What's happened to your body?

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Soon, many kin, many kin in need, will reach my heights.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: We are changing every day. Gladiia. We are one whole. You are of the strongest batch.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: ...Where's my captain?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Tossed into the sea. He was injured pretty badly.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Even their gods were unable to devour Ulpianus. He won't die so easily.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Its body seems to have undergone some changes. It's nothing like the trash we encountered in Sal Viento.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Swordfish? Treating an enemy with caution rather than contempt? Maybe I'm still missing some memories, but does that ever happen, Skadi?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: No, you're right, it is rare. But Seaborn like this were also rare. What kind of prey stands before three Hunters and remains unscathed?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: To be fair, I've barely done anything yet.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: The ship won't hold out if we keep fighting like this, though. It's grown much stronger.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: ...Just the last few blows have already set the lowest deck on fire.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: How dare you treat Garcia and my ship like this! I'll make you regret this, monster.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Please, my kin, even more of our kin call out to me, asking me to maintain the ocean's growth and tranquility.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: If you get in my way, I have no choice but to consume you. I beg of you, return to our kind.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Hey, Amaia.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: ...If you insist on calling me that.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Sure do. Anyway, I just remembered something which REALLY should've been written into those Scriptures—

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: She still owes me her life, and you're going to pay it back.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: A debt? If you are willing to return to our kind, I will grant you that.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: No can do.
The Seaborn does not answer.
It silently leans forward, baring its claws.
In an instant, the damage to the ship's hull passes a critical threshold, and everything in sight shakes violently.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: ...Minutes. Yes, your kind's conception of time. Amaia spoke of this before.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Ten minutes.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: In ten minutes this box will be surrounded by our kin. It will 'sink.'
Hunt and consume. Survive and evolve.
It has never hesitated.
